propositions: The append_event bulk path executes git config user.name once per envelope (6,000 calls over 6,000 events) consuming 47.79s, when a single cached lookup per import would suffice.

The batch_stage_and_commit path calls sweep_stale_staging for every new CREATE ticket (3,000 sweeps), rescanning the same staging root repeatedly while unpublished items remain in the batch, consuming 15.94s.

An identical-state A/B test replacing only the git-config and sweep mechanisms with side-effect-free logical equivalents reduced wall time from 77.23s to 16.40s (60.8s delta, 78.8%), proving these are the dominant avoidable costs and not commit-count or serialization.
The optimization must preserve the locked left-changeful-mamba contract: N=3000 creates, 6,000 events, exactly 24 crash-safe commits, >=10x reduction, rollback, and resume behavior.

Interactive/direct stage_event calls and per-event writes must retain live author lookup and per-call sweep behavior; caching and batching must not leak across independent calls, threads, tasks, or test sessions.

The solution uses import-scoped author caching (contextvar, fallback-keyed, copy-on-write, nested-safe) and at-most-one-sweep-per-batch logic (sweeping only on the first new ticket in a bounded batch) while keeping all direct callers unchanged.
